newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal lifts public sector pay offer to 2.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Portugal lifts public sector pay offer to 2.8 pct.

text.p: Portugal's Socialist government raised its wage offer to public sector unions to 2.8 percent on Monday from 2.6 percent previously, a spokesman said, but the first response from labour leaders was negative.
Leaders of two of three union groups to meet the government on Monday rejected the new offer and the third, the Communist-led Common Front, was certain to follow suit.

"It can only be a rejection," said Bettencourt Picanco of the Union of State Technical Staff (STE), referring to the formal stance his group would take after a meeting to review the government offer on Tuesday.
The STE, which belongs to the Socialist-led General Workers Union confederation, had been pressing for a wage rise of 4.1 percent for next year.

The Common Front issued no immediate statement after the three unions held separate meetings with the government, but it had been seeking the highest increase of the three groups representing Portugal's 500,000 public sector employees.
The government offer was slightly higher than the 2.75 percent that a spokesman had earlier told Reuters would be offered.
The government also undertook to raise the value of benefits, including meal allowances, by the same amount.
A new round of meetings was set for December 17, the spokesman said.
